content:
sam: Hey folks — enterprise customer hitting 401s and bundling errors after upgrading to @redwood/sdk@2.3.1. They say Next.js SSR builds fail in our edge function, but browser calls succeed. Can we triage?

maya: ugh, classic. Any repro steps from their side? package.json, bundler, node version?

sam: They sent minimal repro: Next.js 14 (turbopack enabled), node 18.16, TS 5.4, bundling target 'es2022'. package.json exports look weird. They also see: "invalid_request: malformed auth" only on SSR invocation.

eng-packaging: Can you paste their exports/types fields? Common issue is conditional exports pointing to CJS for "require" and ESM for "import" but bundlers sometimes prefer wrong entry.

sam: Here are the relevant bits they pasted:
```json
{
  "name": "@redwood/sdk",
  "version": "2.3.1",
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.esm.js",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/index.esm.js",
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js"
    },
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  }
}
```

maya: They also shared their server log trace for SSR path: auth header present, then SDK auth middleware returns 401 after parse. But client-side calls (browser fetch) pass.

jordan: Could be that bundler is resolving to the cjs entry in the edge runtime which expects commonjs env (globals) and messing up how the SDK reads env var for API key. Edge runtime sometimes sets process.env differently.

support_lead: Also saw a billing note — they reported unexpected duplicate charges because our retry client retried on 401 transiently? That seems unlikely but worth checking if failed auth triggers token refresh + retry loop.

eng-packaging: Quick tests: some bundlers (turbopack/vite) will rewrite imports to default import from CJS wrappers if not using "exports" fully. The "./package.json" export helps ESM resolution but some older bundlers ignore it. Two quick repro asks: can they build a minimal edge lambda with `node --conditions=import`? Also try forcing `import` path in Next config?

sam: Customer repro steps they gave:
1) npx create-next-app@14 --use-npm
2) npm i @redwood/sdk@2.3.1
3) create pages/api/test-edge.ts that imports `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/sdk'` and calls client.generate in Edge runtime
4) npm run build -> fails with 401 during runtime, and build prints a warning: "Using CommonJS fallback for '@redwood/sdk'"

maya: That warning is our smoking gun. If turbopack falls back to CJS shim, runtime ends up with different env assumptions (no process.env access) and our auth loader returns undefined API key -> 401.

eng-packaging: Proposed short term mitigations for support to suggest: 
- Ask them to pin bundler to use ESM resolution: in next.config.js add `experimental: { esmExternals: true }` or set `webpack: { preferEsmExports: true }` depending on toolchain.
- As a test, ask them to import explicit path: `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/sdk/dist/index.esm.js'` (not ideal but repro helpful).
- Confirm they have PUBLIC_ vs SECRET_ env usage — server-side must use SECRET_API_KEY in Vercel/host provider env.

support_lead: Good. Also get them to run `node -e "console.log(require('./node_modules/@redwood/sdk/package.json').exports)"` in their build container to see resolved exports.

jordan: Longer term: eng-packaging we should add an ESM-only entry and make sure package exports include explicit subpath for `./dist/index.esm.js` as a top-level import - and add `engines` and `conditions` fields that help Turbopack. Also add a `browser` field?

eng-packaging: Noted. I'll open an internal ticket. Quick patch we can push to 2.3.2: add `exports: { ".": {"default": "./dist/index.esm.js", "import":"./dist/index.esm.js", "require":"./dist/index.cjs.js"}, "./package.json": "./package.json" }` and ensure `package.json` includes "type": "module" for ESM builds. But must be careful—changing default can break CJS consumers. Might need a publish with dual packages or clearer docs.

sam: Customer tried the explicit import trick and got rid of 401 in SSR, so that confirms resolution path issue. They asked for a workaround they can keep in prod.

support_lead: For prod: recommend pinning to 2.2.x or vendorizing the ESM file in their repo until we cut 2.3.2. Offer to escalate to account team since this is enterprise.

deploy-bot: deploy status: no canary yet for packaging fix.

eng-packaging: I'll prioritize the patch and include tests for Next.js/Turbopack. Also add a smoke test CI job that builds an edge SSR app and runs basic generate call.

maya: Thanks. I'm going to reply to customer with repro workarounds, ask for build logs and confirm env var names. Will flag for billing team about retry/charge claim and request logs. :thumbsup:

sam: Awesome — keep me posted.

support_lead: Closing loop today — if customer wants immediate help, offer to schedule a short pairing session to update import path and test.

eng-packaging: Created ticket PKG-4215 with notes and linked CI job.

sam: Thanks all. Follow up in #support if we see more customers. :wave:
